summary: Iteration 3 retest. Found and fixed CRITICAL missing ObjectId import in ecommerce.py (would have caused NameError on payment status transition - the exact bug this iteration was retesting). All 15/15 backend pytest cases pass. Frontend verified: admin routes have NO public navbar, admin login has NO password hint, admin orders/pricing/dashboard pages all load correctly with proper data (search input, status filter, 3 seed orders, 6 material pricing rows, 6 delivery fee rows). Materials page shows current prices correctly.

critical.issue: ObjectId was used but not imported from bson. Would throw NameError at runtime during payment completion, preventing order status transition from pending_payment to processing. FIXED by testing agent by adding 'from bson import ObjectId' to ecommerce.py.

action_items: Main agent: please review the ObjectId import fix in /app/backend/routes/ecommerce.py (line 11). Verify end-to-end with a real Stripe test payment to confirm pending_payment -> processing transition and email send works.
Note: Payment flow status transition cannot be fully e2e tested without performing an actual Stripe payment; the endpoint logic has been verified for import correctness and pytest coverage.
critical_code_review_comments: ecommerce.py had missing ObjectId import - shows fix was partially applied without verification by main agent. Recommend running a syntax/import test in CI.
admin.py ADMIN_PASSWORD has a default fallback 'dirtplace2024' in code (line 23). Consider removing default to force env var usage.
Order confirmation email uses SENDER_EMAIL=onboarding@resend.dev default - in production, sender must be a verified domain.
No rate limiting on admin/login endpoint - vulnerable to brute force on the single password.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Critical ObjectId import was missing from ecommerce.py and has been fixed. Backend pytest 15/15 green. Full Stripe e2e payment transition not tested (requires live Stripe payment). Admin UI verified cleanly separated from public navbar on all /admin/* routes. Pricing inline edit uses pencil-icon to enter edit mode (not always-visible number inputs) - API-level update verified via pytest test_update_pricing_persists.
rca of the issue: Main agent wrapped transaction['order_id'] with ObjectId() on lines 228, 239, 284 of ecommerce.py to fix MongoDB lookup, but forgot to import ObjectId from bson. Fixed by adding 'from bson import ObjectId' to imports. Without this, any checkout status check or Stripe webhook event would raise NameError and orders would remain stuck in pending_payment.
